answer: The timber report shows the merge explicitly at each harbor. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Each collapsed cluster gets one marble weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 299 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 118 times the capital for one share.
